name: Thermal Resistance Calculator - R-Value
description: Calculate thermal resistance (R-value and U-value) for composite walls with multiple layers.

seo.title: Thermal Resistance Calculator - R-Value U-Value
seo.description: Calculate thermal resistance for insulation & heat transfer analysis — Series & parallel configurations

formula.explanation: U = 1/R_total. R_total = R_inside + Σ(L_i/k_i) + R_outside. Three material layers provided: L in m, k in W/mK. h in W/m²K.

content.introduction: Calculate the overall heat transfer coefficient (U-value) for a composite wall assembly with up to 3 material layers plus convection resistances on both sides. U-value is the reciprocal of total R-value.

example.description: 100mm brick + 50mm insulation + 10mm plasterboard: U ≈ 0.62 W/m²K (well-insulated wall).

faq.a: Modern insulated walls: 0.2-0.4 W/m²K; roofs: 0.15-0.25; windows: 1.5-3.0; uninsulated solid brick: 2.0-3.0.

faq.q: How do I convert R-value between SI and imperial units?
faq.a: SI R-value (m²·K/W) × 5.678 = imperial R-value (ft²·°F·hr/BTU). For example, 1 m²·K/W = 5.678 ft²·°F·hr/BTU.

faq.q: How do I convert U-value between W/m²·K and BTU/hr·ft²·°F?
faq.a: 1 W/m²·K = 0.1761 BTU/hr·ft²·°F. U = 1/R, so convert R first, then invert to get U in the target unit system.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion for Thermal Resistance
sections.body:
**R-value units**

- 1 m²·K/W = 5.678 ft²·°F·hr/BTU
- 1 ft²·°F·hr/BTU = 0.1761 m²·K/W

**U-value units**

- 1 W/m²·K = 0.1761 BTU/hr·ft²·°F
- 1 BTU/hr·ft²·°F = 5.678 W/m²·K

**Conductivity units**

- 1 W/m·K = 0.578 BTU/hr·ft·°F

R = thickness / k for a single layer; U = 1/R_total for the assembly. Convert all layers to one consistent unit system before summing R-values.
